Crundwell, F.K., Moats, M.S., Ramachandran, V., Robinson, T.G. and Davenport, W.G. (2011). Extractive Metallurgy of Nickel, Cobalt and Platinum Group Metals. Elsevier, Oxford/Amsterdam. ISBN 978-0-08-096809-4. Chapter DOIs of the form 10.1016/B978-0-08-096809-4.100xx-x.

Targeted pass of a 583-page (PDF) metallurgy textbook. Locators are PRINTED page numbers; the PDF copy omits blank and some chapter-opening pages, so the PDF-to-printed offset varies (+6 at the start to -27 at the end). Main file: (1) Chapter 2 cost tables: ferronickel and HPAL mine-to-market project capex per annual t Ni (Tables 2.4, 2.9) and cash opex (Table 2.6, Minara), plus area-share derivations (Tables 2.5, 2.7, 2.10) for the drier, calcination kiln, electric smelting/refining and the HPAL leach/purification area, the latter also converted to per annual t feed using the printed acid ratios (separate process rows); (2) electricity per t feed for every electric smelting furnace with printed data: ferronickel (Table 6.1, plus derived per t Ni as separate process rows), laterite matte (Table 8.1), roasted Ni sulfide calcine incl. Falconbridge-Sudbury and Thompson (Table 17.2), PGM concentrate (Tables 35.2a-b) and slag-cleaning furnaces (Table E.3), with the generic 500 and 800 kWh/t text values; (3) flash smelting electricity per t concentrate derived from MW and t/h (Table 18.1); (4) DC electrowinning energy for Ni and Co derived from printed cell voltage and current efficiency via the Faraday constant (constant not printed - flagged in each note); (5) operating temperatures (temperature-output) for kilns, furnaces, flash smelters, roasters, autoclaves and EW cells. Flows: fuel, reductant, oxygen, electrode and acid consumptions in physical units (kg, L, m3, Nm3, t per t feed) for dewatering kilns (Table 5.1), calcination-reduction kilns (Table 5.2), flash furnaces (Tables 18.1-18.2, derived from hourly rates), electric furnaces and HPAL (acid); heating values are not printed so no GJ conversion was made. Other-values: sulfide mine/concentrator capex (Raglan, Voisey s Bay), whole-chain sulfide Ni and PGM opex with area shares, Cu-Co project costs, campaign lives, carbonyl compressor power, Canadian grinding mill ratings, Caron, Thompson electrorefining and converting notes. Not loaded: Peirce-Smith/TBRC converting (autogenous, blast rates only), hydrogen reduction, carbonyl, PGM refining and solvent extraction chapters (no energy figures), roaster energy (autothermal), steam use in HPAL (not quantified), mineralogy, chemistry and price data. All costs lack a stated price year (study estimates c. 2009-2010, compared with May 2010 LME prices); publication year 2011 used.

(1) Table 2.4 total investment column printed with an extra zero (3 000 000 0000, 2 300 000 0000, 4 000 000 0000); the per-annual-tonne column is consistent with US$ 3.0, 2.5 and 4.2 billion and was used. (2) Table 6.1 Pacific Metals calcine feed printed ambiguously (#1 80, #1 and #2 100 t/h). (3) Table 18.1 offgas row has four values for five smelters (not used). (4) Table 14.2 Sudbury SAG mill 0.3 Mt/a with 8200 kW looks low. (5) Appendix F text refers to anolyte compositions as Table H.3 (should be F.3).
